title: Floral Transition, Photoperiod and Reproductive Morphology

content.overview: Flowering is a developmental transition expressed through changing morphology, not simply the number of days after a schedule switch. Photoperiod response interacts with genotype and plants progress through observable reproductive structures over time.

vocabulary.definition: Developmental shift from predominantly vegetative growth toward reproductive growth.
Duration and timing of light and dark within a daily cycle.
Organized group or cluster of flowers and associated structures.

sections.title: Photoperiod is a developmental signal
sections.body: Cannabis flowering responds strongly to light/dark timing, but cultivar response and morphology should be observed rather than assuming every plant transitions identically.

sections.title: Morphology documents developmental stage
sections.body: Life-cycle characterization research describes progressive changes in leaves, branching and flower development through the cannabis life cycle.

sections.title: Calendar week is supporting metadata
sections.body: Days since photoperiod change are useful records, but actual reproductive morphology and crop response determine biological stage.

workedExamples: Two cultivars flipped on the same date may show reproductive structures at different rates.
A plant showing unexpected delay should trigger checks of light/dark integrity and plant condition rather than automatically changing nutrients.
commonMistakes: Calling every plant week 3 because the calendar says so.
Ignoring light leaks/night interruptions in a delayed flowering diagnosis.
Using flower size alone as stage identity.
content.practicalApplication: Record days since photoperiod change together with repeatable morphological observations at nodes and inflorescences.
content.summary: Advanced flowering records combine photoperiod history with observable reproductive development.
